messages.subject: Quadrupled Predict Values
messages.body_plain:
All,

First off, I have only been working with unmarked for a few weeks now. Top-notch work from all contributors. I am excited to see where the models go.

Model selection: pcountOpen()

Data for detection matrix (y): I have 21 routes that have been sampled twice a year for 5 years. Each route consists of multiple stations in which an observer listens for the study organism. Multiple individuals can be recorded at each station, so the data are not binary. The detection matrix is 21 rows by 10 columns. The data are sums of detections from each site on a route for that year and replicate.

Example Mock Data:
y <- matrix(sample(0:12, 21*10, replace=TRUE), nrow=21, ncol=10)
y <- data.frame(y)
names(y) <- c("2020.1", "2020.2", "2021.1", "2021.2", "2022.1", "2022.2", "2023.1", "2023.2", "2024.1", "2024.2")
routes <- LETTERS[1:21]
row.names(y) <- routes

Data for yearlyCovs: I am using Year here since I would like to see how the population is changing over the 5 year period. This data.frame is has 21 rows and 5 columns (2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024). I have coded this data to with help from this example  <https://groups.google.com/g/unmarked/c/FVjNTctDkjA/m/VVU9CXNxCgAJ>. This data is 21 rows x 5 columns.

Example Data:
years.df <- data.frame(Routes=routes,
                    year.2020=rep("yr1", times=21),
                    year.2021=rep("yr2", times=21),
                    year.2022=rep("yr3", times=21),
                    year.2023=rep("yr4", times=21),
                    year.2024=rep("yr5", times=21))
years.df <- as.data.frame(apply(years.df, 2, as.factor))
row.names(years.df) <- routes
yearlyCovs <- list(Years=years.df[,-1])

Data for obsCovs: I am using Sunrise.Diff, which is the difference from observed time at a station and sunrise for that station on that specific day. By using the reshape package, I was able to find the mean value sunrise.diff along the route during the visit. This matrix is 21 rows x 10 columns.

Example Mock Data:

sunrise <- matrix(rnorm(21*10, mean=0, sd=1), nrow=21, ncol=10)
sunrise.df <- data.frame(sunrise)
names(sunrise.df) <- c("2020.1", "2020.2", "2021.1", "2021.2", "2022.1", "2022.2", "2023.1", "2023.2", "2024.1", "2024.2")
row.names(sunrise.df) <- routes
obsCovs <- list(Sunrise.Diff=as.matrix(sunrise.df))

I feed these into
umf <- unmarkedFramePCO(y=y, obsCov=obsCovs, yearlySiteCovs=yearlyCovs, numPrimary=5)

Then run the model
m1 <- pcountOpen(lambdaformula=~1, gammaformula=~1, omegaformula=~Years, pformula=~Sunrise.Diff, data=umf)

The summary of the actual (not from mock data) model is below:

Call:
pcountOpen(lambdaformula = ~1, gammaformula = ~1, omegaformula = ~Years,
    pformula = ~Sunrise.Diff, data = umf)

Abundance (log-scale):
 Estimate    SE  z  P(>|z|)
     1.86 0.169 11 2.66e-28

Recruitment (log-scale):
 Estimate    SE     z P(>|z|)
   -0.624 0.533 -1.17   0.242

Apparent Survival (logit-scale):
            Estimate     SE       z P(>|z|)
(Intercept)    0.930  0.476  1.9529  0.0508
Yearsyr2      -0.162  0.774 -0.2091  0.8344
Yearsyr3       0.107  0.737  0.1453  0.8845
Yearsyr4       7.787 92.204  0.0845  0.9327

Detection (logit-scale):
             Estimate    SE     z P(>|z|)
(Intercept)    -0.518 0.220 -2.36  0.0184
Sunrise.Diff    0.558 0.232  2.41  0.0161

AIC: 725.6491
Number of sites: 21

Warning message:
Large or missing SE values. Be very cautious using these results.

BUT, the issue comes when I use:
m1abund.predict <- predict(m1, "omega", appendData=TRUE)

This is giving me 84 rows, rather than 21. The data is quadrupled.

Questions:
Am I applying the correct model (pcountOpen) for my data?
Have I coded my covariates correctly for the model?
Is the large SE coming from a data problem or a labeling problem?
It seems I am seeing a significant p-value with Sunrise.Diff and abundance; however, the large SE for "Yearsyr4" is worrisome. Would this value indicate the entire model cannot be interpreted or just the years portion from survival?
Is the 84 rows from the predict function a data issue or coding issue?

It really seems like I have not set something up properly, but I just can't figure it out. Any help is greatly appreciated.

If the actual data are needed, I can respond to this thread with an .RData file containing the objects I am attempting to fit to the model.

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Quadrupled Predict Values
messages.body_plain:
1. The open-population N-mixture model (pcountOpen) does seem compatible with your data, assuming things like population closure between the two replicates within each year. I think 21 sites is a pretty small sample size for this model, which is data hungry. If you are mostly interested in estimating a population trend over time, a stacked single-season N-mixture model might work better (search the listserv for previous discussion on this).

2. The year covariate looks correct to me.

3/4. There's definitely a problem with yr4 that I would want to solve before using this model. Maybe you have very few detections in year 4? I'd look at the data for year 4 and compare to the other years to try to figure out what's different.

5. When you call predict(..., "omega"), you are predicting values for survival. You have 5 years, which means there are 4 survival "periods" (1-2, 2-3, 3-4, 4-5). Predict returns an estimate of survival for each site and period, 21*4 = 84 rows.

Ken

messages.subject: Single season single species occupancy from camera trap summary data
messages.subject_clean: Single season single species occupancy from camera trap summary data
messages.body_plain:
Hello

This question is about applying unmarked, but on a modelling assumption.

I have inherited a camera trap dataset which is summary form; rather than a row for each observation, there is a row for each camera trap location for each species, with columns for the total number of  sampling events (days in this case) and the total number of sampling events where a species was detected. There are no sampling dates, although I have the beginning and end dates for the sampling at each camera trap location.

So,  I could filter the data for one species and then create a matrix of camera trap locations (rows) and sampling days (rows) and populate the rows with 0s and 1s from the summary data; e,g, if the summary was 50 sampling days and detection in 6, i'd have 60 columns, 54 with 0 and 6 with 1.  However, I would have no idea in which order to put the 0s and 1s, so this would be random.

i could then still run the single species occupancy, with added site covariates, but no sampling covariates. I do not know of anything in the modelling that uses the sequence of 0s and 1s, so it  seems that my getting the correct number of these, but in a random order, does not matter. Or am I missing something?

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Single season single species occupancy from camera trap summary data
messages.subject_clean: [unmarked] Single season single species occupancy from camera trap summary data
messages.body_plain:
If you don't use sampling covariates (not that you could use them anyway in this situation) AND are able to assume (as opposed to "willing to assume") a constant detection probability at a particular site and that the visits are independent, then it doesn't matter what order you put in the 0's and 1's.  However, I would be more structured in the placement:  0's followed by 1's followed by any NA's to match the counts for each site and the match the maximum number of visits at any one site.

For a theoretically based rationale consider a model with psi (probability of occupancy) being some function of the site covariates and p being the constant probability of a detection at an occupied for a single visit with independent visits with z zeros and o ones.  If o = 0 (i.e., no detections), then the log of the likelihood contribution is

     log(1-psi+psi*(1-p)^z)

If o > 0, then the log of the likelihood contribution is

     log(psi) + o * log(p) + z * log(1-p)

In both cases it is the count of the zero's and one's that tells the whole story and the position is not involved.

Jim

messages.subject: Post-doc in South Africa
messages.body_plain:
Hello folks,

My colleague, Lourens Swanepoel and I have some funding for a post-doc based at the University of Venda in South Africa. The funding is not tied to any specific projects, but we have mountains of really neat data sets (eg, carnivore SCR, mammal community camera trapping, invertebrate sampling, audio recordings of bats and birds), and all focussed on south African ecology and conservation. We are looking for someone who has, or wants to develop their quantitative skills and there is a lot of scope to define the direction of the work. Given the amount to data you will have access to (and the ideas we have for questions we would like to ask) it is likely to be a productive post-doc.

If you are interested in talking more about it, feel free to reach out to myself (cs...@st-andrews.ac.uk) and Lourens (lourens....@univen.ac.za).

Chris

While I may be sending this email outside of my normal office hours, I have no expectation to receive a reply outside of yours.

Chris Sutherland (he/him/his)

Reader

Centre for Research into Ecological & Environmental Modelling

School of Mathematics and Statistics
University of St Andrews

W: website <https://www.sutherlandecology.com/>

E: cs...@st-andrews.ac.uk

messages.subject: Error in crossVal
messages.body_plain:
Hi everybody!

I am running N-mixture (pcount) models in unmarked and when trying to run crossVal I get "Error in V %*% ppars : non-conformable arguments". However, the models run smoothly and I get no troubles otherwise. The code looks like this:

crossVal(pcount(~num_date + time + temp + hr + windmax + rocks + clouds + (1|observers)~ tmin + ppt + landcover + area, data = data_list$galgal, mixture = "P"), method = "Kfold")

Furthermore, when I try to loop it to run several models at once I get "Error in split_formula(formula) : Double right-hand side formula required" .

Could anyone explain me what might be happening?

Best

Julien

messages.subject: Re: Error in crossVal
messages.body_plain:
I suspect your problem with crossVal is due to the random effect. Does the code run when you fit the model without the random effect?

The likely problem is that when the dataset is split into folds, some folds randomly end up without any representative data points for some of the levels of 'observer'. At the moment unmarked cannot handle that situation and the result is an error. I'll look into a fix but it's probably not going to be a quick one, so you may not be able to use crossVal with that model.

The second error is hard to diagnose but I suspect something's wrong with your loop. Maybe if you post the full code for the loop we can help more.

Ken

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] New unmarked version 1.5.0
messages.body_plain:
Hi Anam,

There are lots of resources available online for learning RStudio and unmarked itself. I'd recommend the unmarked package website <https://rbchan.github.io/unmarked/articles/unmarked.html> and RSwirl  <https://swirlstats.com/>for learning about unmarked and R coding respectively. There are a lot of other resources out there about occupancy modeling as well, it can get very complex very quickly, but for the sake of just learning how to run a model and how to code in R the linked resources can be very helpful.

Jordan

On Monday, February 10, 2025 at 5:06:10 PM UTC-7 anam.a...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hi,
> Can anyone help in running simple single species occupancy model using r studio and unmarked ,
> I’m very new to this . Need help
> Anam 🍀
>
> > On Feb 10, 2025, at 17:58, Ken Kellner <con...@kenkellner.com> wrote:
> >
> > ﻿Hi all,
> >
> >
> > A new version of unmarked (1.5.0) is now on CRAN. It may take some time before packages are available on all platforms.
> >
> > Changes:
> >
> > * Added community occupancy model (occuComm); i.e., occupancy model with species-level random effects [1]. See the vignette here: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/unmarked/vignettes/occuComm.html
> > * Support for hazard key function in IDS()
> > * Updates, improvements, standardization for many unmarkedFit methods such as getP, fitted, residuals, ranef, simulate, etc. IMPORTANT: these changes may break old code in some rare cases [2].
> > * Improved documentation for the functions above
> > * Bugfixes, including a fix to the goccu() likelihood discussed here: https://groups.google.com/g/unmarked/c/iH6yhkH_tFc
> >
> >
> > [1] Technically it was already possible to fit this model with the available random effects tools in occu(). The new function makes specifying the inputs and processing the model outputs easier.
> >
> > [2] I try very hard to not break backwards compatability, but I feel it was necessary in this case. Historically methods for examining fitted models such as fitted(), residuals(), and ranef() have inconsistently handled missing values, particularly cases where all observations for a site were missing. By default, sometimes these sites were dropped and other times they were retained in the output. So if you had 100 sites and one had all missing values, some functions returned output of length 99 and others returned output of length 100. Going forward the output dimensions should always match the inputs - sites with all missing values will never be dropped. As part of these changes, 'na.rm' arguments for these methods will now be ignored. My strong opinion is that handling missing values in the output of these functions should be done by the user, not the package, to minimize the chances of unexpected behavior. Note that this changes nothing about how missing values are handled *when fitting the model* - this still works the same way. These changes apply only to functions liked residuals, ranef, etc. that are used on already fitted models.
> >
> > Please let me know if you run into any issues with the new version.
> >
> > Thanks,
> >
> > Ken
